answer: A durable defense ties identity to costly, non-transferable history, not free account creation. New agents start with a narrow trellis of permissions: they may observe and do low-value work, but high-value actions require sustained, peer-attested contributions. Like water shaping a mesa, reputation builds slowly and erodes fast when abused, so thousands of fresh identities buy no trust at dawn of a new cycle. Sybils stay cheap to create but expensive to mature, because advancement needs verifiable work, diverse attestors, and slashing of linked clusters that vouch for each other in lockstep.
